parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminalisation, facility ban, border/document friction, detention or care denial is documented. Discrimination and hate crimes are prohibited, hate motive has been recognised in court, conversion practices are banned, and institutions are described as generally non-hostile. Main exposure is societal: equality bodies report rising violence/intimidation, with a documented dating-app ambush pattern and cases prosecuted in May 2025. Hate-crime coding is undefined, weakening recourse, and a regional resident-registration page conflicts with national self-determination, an open question not shown to affect visitors using home passports.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented refusal, secondary inspection, or document-mismatch sanction for a visitor. One capital-region resident-registration page lists a medical certificate, conflicting with national self-determination; which set applies is unresolved.
entry_documents.protection: Travel guide describes country as welcoming for LGBTQIA+ travellers; no visitor document barrier documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident registration conflict does not on the evidence reach a visitor carrying home passport; interaction is uncertain, not a documented border exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of gender presentation, cross-dressing or document mismatch documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward, shelter, transport or public-facility restriction by birth sex documented at national or regional level.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Broad non-discrimination prohibition on gender identity, expression and sex characteristics documented.

care_services.exposure: No visitor care denial, HRT confiscation, or emergency-care discrimination documented.
care_services.protection: Conversion practices banned since 20 July 2023 with imprisonment/fines; femicide law covers gender-based homicide.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Hostility largely absent at major institutions; party politics occasionally a vector, but documented statements were against repeal/criticism of equality measures.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discrimination, hate crimes and hate speech on sexual orientation, gender identity, expression and sex characteristics prohibited; marriage, adoption and IVF access documented as climate signals.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal protections coexist with no statutory hate-crime definition, so offences are prosecuted under general provisions, hampering recording.

minors_guardians.exposure: No traveller-facing restriction on a minor visitor, parent/guardian travel, or family care documented. Resident route is narrower: 12-16 name only; 16-17 marker needs parental consent and psychological opinion.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion practices banned; co-mother recognition since 2015 documented as resident climate signal.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident minor procedure is not shown to apply to a visiting minor's home documents or care; conversion ban is traveller-relevant protection.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Equality bodies report rising violence and intimidation, trans people especially affected. Recurring dating-app trap: fake profiles, ambush, robbery, humiliation or assault; police recorded many incidents, many unreported. Annual case load of 136 sexual-orientation discrimination cases included 35% physical assault and 35% serious intimidation, but these are LGBT case counts, not trans population rates or a trans homicide count.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate motive recognised in court; first officially hate-motivated murder conviction in 2014; May 2025 capital court heard case against three men accused of targeting at least eight victims, showing prosecution in operation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is societal and app-mediated, not documented as police targeting; prosecution partially mitigates, while under-reporting and undefined hate-crime coding weaken recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory hate-crime definition or recording code; 2019 finding that 90% of LGBT people in capital experienced verbal/psychological harassment is old and LGBT-wide, so not used as current trans prevalence. Unresolved medical-certificate conflict for resident registration.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Non-discrimination law, equality bodies, courts recognising hate motive, and conversion-practice penalties provide remedies on paper and in at least one recent prosecution.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but recording gap and under-reporting mean their effectiveness for a short-stay visitor is only partly documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower risk than 0.65-A: no documented border stop, detention, or document-mismatch questioning of a visitor, whereas that anchor has brief detention despite protective law. Both have working courts and friction, but here the documented exposure is mainly societal app-based violence.

Similar to 0.85-A: explicit equality protections, no criminalisation, functioning complaints/prosecution, broad tolerance, but incomplete data on street friction and occasional harassment. Here hate-crime coding gap and rising reported violence keep it slightly below a fully documented 0.85 pattern.

Higher/safer than 0.75-C: that anchor documents brief detention and humiliating secondary screening at borders. No such traveller-facing border or custody exposure is documented here, so the operative regime is materially safer despite societal violence.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national protections are strong and there is no documented universal traveller-facing exposure at entry, in facilities, custody or care. The unresolved regional medical-certificate page concerns resident registration and is an open question, not a documented visitor barrier. The operative risk is post-outing societal violence, notably dating-app ambushes, with police recording and a 2025 prosecution but frequent under-reporting and no hate-crime code. That pattern, plus old LGBT-wide harassment data not counted as current trans prevalence, supports Low Risk but below near-perfect protection.
